Visiting

From Padang to Pantai Carocok

Pantai Carocok is in Painan, Pesisir Selatan Regency, several hours of overland travel from Padang. This page summarises sensible options and limits to confirm, not fixed schedules.

Updated · 28 Oktober 2026

Air gateway

Minangkabau Airport (PDG)

Minangkabau International Airport in the Padang area is the main air gateway to Pantai Carocok. From the airport, continue by hired vehicle, licensed taxi, or other transport heading south.

Not a short transfer

Painan is a fair distance from the airport; allow buffer time for rest, meals and traffic, not just the map distance.

Overland

Along the Padang–Painan corridor

The overland trip follows the west-coast arterial road and turns toward the south coast. Travel time depends heavily on weather, traffic, and road conditions; we do not quote a fixed number because it can vary materially.

  • Use a private or rented vehicle if you want stop flexibility.
  • A taxi or ride app can be arranged from Padang, but confirm the estimate before boarding.
  • Avoid very tight schedules; the coast road is busy on weekends and holidays.

Drop-off

Arriving in Painan

Tell the driver “Pantai Carocok, Painan”. The beach is on the western side of central Painan; the remaining route from town is covered on a separate page.

Questions

Before you go

01How long from Padang to Pantai Carocok?+

We do not quote a fixed number because travel time depends on weather, traffic and road conditions. Plan several hours of overland travel with buffer, not just map distance.

02Is there a direct Padang–Carocok bus?+

Availability of a direct bus service all the way to the beach is unverified. Check active departure points and schedules with transport operators before relying on a direct route.

03Car rental or ride app?+

A rental gives flexibility to stop along the coast. A ride app is convenient for a point-to-point trip, but confirm availability and fare before boarding.

04Is self-driving safe?+

The main route is passable, but take care on coastal bends and in rain. Fuel up before entering the coast where petrol stations are sparse.
